newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish policeman shot dead in Basque ETA attack.
newsitem.headline: Spanish policeman shot dead in Basque ETA attack.

text.p: A Spanish police officer was killed in the northern Basque region on Saturday in what officials said was an attack by ETA separatist guerrillas.
The officials said Jose Manuel Garcia, 43, was shot in the head by an unidentified gunman in a restaurant in the Basque town of Zierbana and died immediately.
Witnesses told local radio that a lone gunman entered the restaurant and shot Garcia in the back of the head while he was dining with his wife. The attacker then fled by car.
"This was clearly an attack by ETA due to the nature and target of the attack," said a regional government source.
The separatist group has often targeted members of the security forces and police in its 29-year struggle for an independent Basque state.
In a similar attack last week, ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) was blamed for killing a police inspector outside his home in the Basque city of Bilbao.

Just hours before Saturday's attack, Spain's Interior Minister Jaime Mayor Oreja praised the progress security forces had made against ETA rebels and said he felt the group was going through a period of decline. ETA has killed some 800 people since 1968.

"I believe this year has...served to make clear that ETA is going through a period of decay, of decline, and without doubt this year they have had numerous failures in what is an attempt to revive this phenomenon in the Basque Country," Oreja told state radio.
"That is why they have become more radicalised in certain circumstances," he said.
